transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Lena Ortiz, Marcus Chen, Priya Nair (Redwood) — Daniel Park, Marta Ruiz, Omar El-Sayed (Oceanic)

Summary:
Quick compliance-focused workshop to validate what admin telemetry Redwood captures by default, export/connectors (SIEM/S3/Kafka), retention options, KMS key ownership patterns, and SOC2/ISO evidence for Oceanic Systems' governance needs. Agreed to run a pilot export to their Splunk and enumerate required audit fields.

Topics:
- What events are captured (admin console, API keys, token use, role changes)
- Export options (streaming to SIEM, batch S3 exports, webhook)
- Retention & archival policies (default, custom, legal holds)
- Encryption & KMS (customer-managed keys vs Redwood-managed)
- RBAC/SSO audit trails and SSO session logs
- Evidence artifacts for SOC2/ISO assessments

Action items (captured in metadata above).

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, i'm lena from Redwood, i know we have a packed agenda — the goal is to make sure we cover exactly what Oceanic needs for audit and compliance, ok?
[00:12] Daniel: yep, thanks lena, i'm daniel — ciso — i'll kick things off with our key constraints: we need immutable admin logs for 7 years for certain products, 3 years for others, and the logs must be exportable to our splunk cluster in eu-west region; also, keys need to be under our KMS, ideally HSM-backed.
[00:30] Marcus: thanks daniel, that's helpful — quick note: we support both streaming and batched exports; streaming to syslog/kafka/splunk is fine and we also have S3 snapshot exports for long-term archival.
[00:45] Marta: quick clarifying q, when you say "admin logs" do you capture console UI actions, or only API events? we need both so we can link UI actions to user sessions.
[00:58] Marcus: good question — by default we capture both API and console admin events. so things like role grants, policy changes, model pinning, dedicated capacity changes, token creation/deletion — those are included. there are also session-level logs for sso sign-ins but sometimes the identity provider attributes can be sparsely transcribed in our raw events.
[01:20] Omar: you mentioned token creation — do you capture the token value? we can't have tokens in logs.
[01:25] Marcus: no, we never log secret values. we log token ID and metadata (who created, when, scope) but not the secret. sometimes transcripts show token-values as redacted or as "[REDACTED]" in our UI exports — automated redaction.
[01:40] Daniel: ok good. on encryption, can we bring our own key with HSM?
[01:45] Lena: short answer yes for Private deployments — customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; for Hosted API we offer a BYOK path for certain enterprise customers but there are operational caveats — i'll send the KMS whitepaper.
[01:58] Marta: and for the streaming exports, is the data encrypted in transit and at rest on the export target?
[02:03] Marcus: TLS for in-transit, and we can sign/encrypt the payloads. On S3 exports, if you provide a bucket with SSE-KMS we don't re-encrypt — we upload the files already encrypted with your key if you configure the BYOK flow.
[02:22] Daniel: what does the schema look like? we need fields for actor, actor_role, ip_address, user_agent, action_type, target_resource, before/after delta, request_payload_hash, request_id, correlate_id, timestamp — can you show an example event?
[02:36] Marcus: yeah, i'll paste a sample JSON later, but short verbal: each event has a core header (event_id, ts, service, region), actor identity block (id, email, idp), action details (verb, target_type, target_id), outcome (success/fail/code), and an optional before/after snapshot for config changes — big changes we snapshot the object and store diffs. note: big diffs are truncated and full object snapshots are stored in the archive blob with a pointer in the event.
[03:05] Marta: truncation is concerning for forensics — is there a way to ensure full object capture for certain workflows?
[03:10] Marcus: yes — there's a policy flag per-tenant where we can force full snapshots for specified resource types; this costs more storage but we can include that in the pilot scope.
[03:24] Daniel: retention and legal hold — can we set retention per-resource and stop deletion if a legal hold is placed?
[03:30] Priya: yep, we have retention tiers: default short-term (90d), extended (1y, 3y, 7y) and archive. we also support holds which freeze deletion, and audit exports include metadata for holds. holds can be set via API or Console and are visible in the export events.
[03:49] Omar: for the export pipeline to splunk — do you push events natively or do we pull from S3? what's the latency?
[03:55] Marcus: streaming push to Splunk via HTTP Event Collector typical latency is sub-second to a few seconds. S3 batch exports run hourly/daily depending on size. for compliance real-time monitoring you should do streaming; for long-term retention archive to S3 and Glacier.
[04:12] Daniel: any PII in the admin events — usernames, emails ok, but we need to avoid personal details in payloads.
[04:18] Marcus: by default actor email is included, we can pseudonymize or hash PII on export if you need a policy. we also support field-level redaction rules.
[04:28] Marta: when you say "actor" — do you support external identities from SSO, like SAML attributes?
[04:33] Marcus: yes, we ingest idp attributes (subject, email, groups) but sometimes attribute names are mapped differently depending on the idp config; we'll show mapping examples.
[04:46] Daniel: SOC2 evidence — what artifacts can you provide for an auditor?
[04:50] Lena: we provide a package: SOC2 report, control matrix mapping, sample audit logs for chosen date ranges (redacted), RBAC policy exports, and encryption key management procedures. for Private customers we can also provide network diagrams and HSM attestation docs. i'll attach the bundle after the call.
[05:08] Daniel: great. how about ISO27001? any additional docs?
[05:11] Lena: ISO Annex A mappings and our ISMS summary are available; i'll include them.
[05:18] Marta: do you surface who did a canary/rollback in the audit? we need to know who triggered a deploy rollback — is that in the event payload?
[05:25] Marcus: yes, deploy/rollbacks are events with before/after and user id, plus a correlate_id linking to the CI system if integrated. we have hooks for common CI like GitHub Actions or GitLab to include pipeline ids.
[05:40] Omar: curious on RBAC — can you export role definitions and assignments regularly? we need snapshots of role assignments for point-in-time evidence.
[05:47] Marcus: yep, we can export role and policy graph regularly; snapshots are stored as objects and referenced in audit events. we also have an API to request an on-demand snapshot and a scheduled snapshot cadence (daily/weekly).
[06:05] Daniel: for the pilot, i'd like to see a minimal set of fields and then expand. recommended minimal: timestamp, actor_id, actor_email_hash, action, target, outcome, request_id, correlate_id, region, retention_tier.
[06:18] Marcus: noted — will provide schema plus sample events.
[06:25] [10:00 segment ellided for brevity — discussion about VPC endpoints, private link, and customer network egress rules]
[18:42] Marta: question on access logs for console — do you capture session durations and MFA events?
[18:48] Marcus: session start/stop and MFA challenge events are captured; we include device/user agent and IP; for geo-ip we provide best-effort geolocation.
[19:05] Daniel: needs to be EU-only processing for some products — can you pin region?
[19:11] Lena: yes for Private we support EU-only; for Hosted API we have region-aware hosting and data residency controls — you can request EU-only tenancy and we will route data accordingly.
[19:25] Omar: regarding KMS — if we use our own key, who rotates it and how do we provide rotation proofs?
[19:33] Marcus: rotation remains under your control for customer-managed keys; we log key-use events (wrap/unwrap) and you can export key rotation history as part of the KMS audit. for Redwood-managed keys we rotate per our policy and provide rotation logs in the evidence pack.
[19:50] Daniel: legal hold use-case: if legal places a hold, how do we surface that across the exports?
[19:55] Priya: the hold flag is part of the object metadata and events referencing the object include hold_status, hold_initiator, hold_timestamp — exports will include that field so downstream SIEMs can mark the record.
[20:10] Marta: does Redwood sign exported files so we can verify integrity later?
[20:15] Marcus: yes we support optional payload signing; we can provide a detached signature per export batch which you can verify with our public key or integrate into your archival verification.
[20:27] Daniel: audit trail chain of custody — do you provide a manifest for batches?
[20:31] Marcus: each batch includes a manifest with counts, checksums, timestamp window, and a signature.
[20:36] Omar: curious about performance impact — if we enable full snapshots and longer retention for certain resource types, will that impact latency?
[20:44] Marcus: minimal impact on request latency — snapshots are taken asynchronously and stored to cold storage; CPU/IO for snapshotting can affect throughput at extreme scale but we can throttle snapshot jobs and schedule low-load windows. dedicated customers can provision more capacity.
[21:05] Daniel: for the pilot we want to stress test with a sample 24h of production-like events — can Redwood replay or generate synthetic events?
[21:13] Marcus: we have a replay harness and a synthetic generator; we'll prepare a replay that matches your traffic shape.
[21:21] Lena: quick check — is there any blocker for Oceanic to run a small pilot?
[21:26] Omar: main blocker is KMS confirmation — we need to see flow for BYOK; also need the sample schema to validate mapping to Splunk.
[21:35] Lena: action: we'll send the KMS whitepaper and a sample schema + sample JSON. Marcus will prepare the replay plan.
[21:42] [30:00 - 45:00 more detailed technical Q/A: mapping idp attributes, SAML/SCIM provisioning logs, examples of redaction policies, how to correlate user sessions across idp and console, and a brief walkthrough of the Redwood Console export UI — transcript contains some ASR artifacts and brief crosstalk]
[45:07] Marta: last question — for auditors, can you provide a time-series of admin changes for a 6-month window as a signed bundle?
[45:15] Marcus: yes, we can generate a signed archive for any time window, with manifest and checksums. for sensitive change events we can include full snapshots if requested.
[45:30] Daniel: timeline — we want pilot started by April 20 and run 2 weeks. can you meet that?
[45:36] Lena: yes that's feasible.
[45:40] Priya: i'll set up the pilot board and invite stakeholders.
[45:45] Omar: ok, last ops question — retention deletions: is there an immutable delete? meaning once retention expires, can an admin still delete?
[45:55] Marcus: deletions respect retention and holds. admins cannot delete data before retention expiry unless they have an explicit override role which is auditable. we recommend locking-down override access and we log any use of overrides.
[46:12] Daniel: great. any compliance exceptions or known gaps?
[46:16] Lena: evolving areas are deep packet capture of agent telemetry — we don't capture full network packets; if you need pcap level for forensic you'd need an on-prem tap. we'll document the limits.
[46:30] Marta: noted.
[46:35] Lena: all right let's recap and list next steps.
[46:40] Lena: recap: 1) Lena to share SOC2/ISO bundle + KMS whitepaper; 2) Marcus to share schema, sample events, and export manifest examples; 3) Marcus+Omar to design Splunk ingestion pilot and replay plan; 4) Oceanic to provide retention requirements and list of systems in scope. Pilot to start week of 2026-04-20.
[47:05] Daniel: good recap, thanks.
[47:10] Omar: thanks everyone.
[47:15] Lena: we'll follow up with calendar invites and doc links. thanks all.
[47:22] [call ends]
